subject: RFP Clarifications: Misuse Detection, Alerting & Escalation Workflow
messages:
From: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@finserve.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@finserve.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Misuse Detection & Reporting — Clarifications

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the RFP response packet. The security team reviewed the sections on monitoring and incident reporting and had a few clarifying requests before we finalize scoring: 

1) Detection coverage: Can you itemize which categories of misuse (fraud, disallowed financial advice, phishing generation, personal data exfiltration prompts) are covered by Redwood's automated detectors versus manual review triggers? We need an SLA for detection-to-notification for severity P0/P1/P2.

2) Alerting & evidence: For a flagged interaction, what exact artifacts are retained and for how long (prompt, response, KV cache snapshot, model version, request metadata, IP/region)? Which of these are available via API for downstream ingestion?

3) Escalation path: Provide a short escalation workflow mapping (automated alert -> analyst triage -> engineering takehome) including expected RTTs and the roles involved. If you have a sample playbook, please attach.

4) False positives & governance: What controls exist to tune sensitivity per-account, and how do you surface model/regression changes that might increase false positives?

Can you get answers back by end-of-day Wednesday (2027-08-18)? Procurement is waiting on an evidence bundle.

Best,
Alice Ramos
Senior Security Engineer — FinServe

--
FinServe Security Team
security@finserve.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramos <alice.ramos@finserve.com>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@finserve.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Misuse Detection & Reporting — Clarifications

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the detailed asks — appreciate the specificity. I've summarized answers below and attached a matrix + playbook PDF with concrete examples. Highlights:

1) Detection coverage
- Automated detectors (real-time): disallowed content classes (policy matches), prompt/response toxicity heuristics, known prompt signatures for fraud/phishing.
- Heuristic & model-based scoring: uses ensemble of policy classifier + behavioral anomaly model for rapid triage.
- Manual review triggers: high-confidence fraud indicators, legal/PII exfiltration flags, and incidents where confidence is medium but triggered across multiple signals.
- SLA (detection -> notification): P0 (critical, active exploitation) = 5 minutes, P1 (high risk) = 30 minutes, P2 (low-to-medium) = 4 hours — these are for Dedicated customers; hosted API customers get alerting via webhooks with similar SLAs depending on plan.

2) Alerting & evidence
- Artifacts retained per incident: full request (prompt + metadata), model response, model id + weights tag, top-K token log (sampling), KV cache snapshot (where applicable), request headers (including region), and routing decisions.
- Retention windows configurable per account: default 90 days; options for 180/365 with enterprise contract.
- API access: incident list, evidence bundle download (JSONL), and streaming webhooks for new alerts. See attached audit_log_sample_snippet.txt for schema example.

3) Escalation path (summary)
- Automated detection -> Alert (<5m for P0) -> Redwood Triage Queue -> Customer-configured analyst/CS notification via webhook/Slack -> Analyst reviews evidence (15–60m) -> If confirmed, Redwood Engineering engages for mitigation/rollback (RTT 2–6 hours depending on severity).
- Roles: Redwood Detection Engine, Redwood Triage Analysts, Customer CS/Security ops, Redwood Engineering on-call.
- Playbook attached: escalation_playbook_redwood_v2.pdf (contains runbooks, mitigation play options, and sample timeline templates).

4) False positives & governance
- Per-account sensitivity profiles: threshold tuning, allow/deny lists, and model override pins.
- Regression monitoring: We run daily baseline drift checks and weekly evals against customer-provided test prompts; any model change that increases false positives above configured thresholds triggers an automatic rollback to previous model and an incident review.

Attachments included: misuse_monitoring_matrix_v3.xlsx, escalation_playbook_redwood_v2.pdf, audit_log_sample_snippet.txt

I'll loop in Ben and Laura for any additional security/ops specifics. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the matrix tomorrow.

Best,
--
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: RFP: Misuse Detection & Reporting — Clarifications

Adding a few implementation specifics for FinServe to include in the evidence bundle: 

- Detection telemetry export: we can provide a Kafka-compatible feed (TLS + mTLS) for high-volume customers; for smaller customers we support S3 export of daily incident bundles.
- SLA exceptions: for P0 we commit to 99.9% availability on alerting pipeline; mitigation actions (model rollback) are on a best-effort basis depending on model artifacts and infra.
- Redaction options: PII/HIPAA-sensitive artifacts can be redacted at ingestion with a reversible token map for authorized audits.

Also suggested wording for the RFP response (Procurements): "Redwood provides configurable detection profiles, an evidence API, and a documented escalation playbook. Production customers may request extended retention and an integrated telemetry export for SIEM ingestion."

Laura, can you confirm that the playbook PDF includes the triage checklist and the contact matrix? If so, Soojin, we should send the updated bundle to Alice tomorrow morning with the Kafka export note and a short proposed MSA addendum for telemetry retention.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
